parent_v25.key_result: 12/45 v24 hidden-age residual rows changed lag-2 mature state, while six design rows had age differences but mature-state invariance

scientific_question: Which qualitative properties of an age-dependent present-state mapping determine whether hidden colonization-history differences remain ecologically visible or are erased?

latent_rows.reuse: the exact 384 v21-v25 directed landscapes, clustered/dispersed three-source sets, three activation histories, first-arrival maps and common present horizon T*

history_blind_occupancy.rule: state(node)=1 for every reached equilibrium non-source node
history_blind_occupancy.purpose: negative control that deliberately erases all colonization-age information

persistent_threshold_lag2.purpose: exact v25 mature-state process; monotone persistent memory

transient_window_age1_2.purpose: non-monotone transient memory that is present only during an intermediate age window

saturating_age_class_cap3.purpose: multistate monotone memory with finite saturation

information_relation.history_blind_occupancy: constant over all reached equilibrium non-source nodes

primary_outputs: history-equivalence-class count under each process for every design row
rows with any history-dependent present-state difference under each process
v24 hidden-age residual rows detected by each process
v25 threshold-invariant age-different rows detected by transient or saturating process
rows where threshold and transient process disagree on whether history matters
rows where saturating cap3 still erases exact age differences
unique-origin versus confluence memory under each process

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: The history-blind occupancy process has one present-state class in every design row.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: Any violation is an implementation/theory failure.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: For every design row, saturating-age-class class count is <= exact first-arrival/colonization-age class count.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: Any violation is an implementation/theory failure.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: For every design row, saturating-age-class class count is >= persistent-threshold and >= transient-window class count.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: Any violation is an implementation/theory failure.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: At least one design row has different transient-window present-state maps across activation histories.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if the transient process is history-invariant everywhere.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: At least one design row is history-dependent under persistent threshold but not transient window, and at least one other row is history-dependent under transient window but not persistent threshold.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if either direction of process-specific disagreement is absent.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: At least one age-different but persistent-threshold-invariant design row becomes history-dependent under transient window or saturating age class.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if all v25 threshold-hidden age differences remain invisible under both richer processes.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: At least one design row has different exact age maps but identical saturating-age-class maps.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if cap3 state preserves every exact age difference.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: Among the 45 v24 hidden-age residual rows, at least two frozen non-control processes differ in which rows they classify as present-state-history-dependent.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if all non-control processes mark exactly the same v24 hidden-age residual rows.

secondary_outputs: pairwise Jaccard overlap among row sets showing memory under each process
process-specific mean fraction of non-source nodes with history-dependent state
process-specific memory by clustered/dispersed source geometry
target compression relative to exact age and exact activation history
claim_boundary: The four processes are synthetic qualitative classes, not calibrated demographic models.
The transient window and cap3 levels are frozen experimental mappings rather than fitted biological thresholds.
A process-family difference shows target dependence of historical legacy, not empirical prevalence of any real ecological mechanism.
No abundance, extinction, density dependence, evolution or biotic feedback is introduced.
stop_rules: Do not change lag2, transient-window bounds or cap3 after scoring.
Do not add a fifth process to rescue a failed hypothesis.
Do not tune process rules by clustered/dispersed result.
Do not change T* after scoring.
